financial_flags.finding: Revenue has declined two years running: $2.70B (FY24) to $2.49B (FY25) to $2.45B (FY26).
financial_flags.why: Profitability has been achieved through cost cuts rather than top-line growth, which may limit sustainability.

financial_flags.finding: Total liabilities ($2.196B) exceed total assets ($2.056B), a stockholders' deficit of roughly $140M (derived), though the gap has narrowed from FY25.
financial_flags.why: Thin equity cushion; reliance on debt financing.

financial_flags.finding: Long-term debt of $1.33B against $1.21B cash; the first profit ($63.2M) is small relative to interest expense cited in the 10-K ($123.8M, one of the periods reported).
financial_flags.why: Interest burden is heavy relative to earnings; profits are thin.

financial_flags.finding: Cash rose from $697.6M to $1.21B over two years and debt fell from $1.55B to $1.33B.
financial_flags.why: Liquidity and deleveraging are improving, which is a positive.

risks.finding: Profitability is new and may not be sustained; the company has a history of operating losses.
risks.evidence_quote: Although we reported net income in fiscal year 2026, we have incurred significant operating losses in prior periods and may not be able to sustain profitability

risks.finding: Credit facility covenants include a minimum liquidity of $250M and minimum Subscription Revenue of $1.2B (when revolver is drawn). Total debt is about $1.3B, including $350M of 5.50% convertible notes due 2029.
risks.evidence_quote: requires us, when revolving loans are outstanding, to maintain a total level of liquidity of not less than $250.0 million

risks.finding: Ongoing class action, personal injury, and regulatory proceedings tied to Tread+ and Bike recalls. A new Bike+ recall was announced in November 2025.
risks.evidence_quote: We have been and in some cases continue to be subject to class action litigation, private personal injury claims and other regulatory proceedings

risks.finding: Product recalls (Tread+ 2021, Bike 2023, Bike+ Nov 2025) may bring further material costs, and insurance may not cover them.
risks.evidence_quote: in November 2025, in collaboration with the CPSC and Health Canada, we announced a voluntary recall of certain Original Series Bike+ units

risks.finding: Sole reliance on contract manufacturers, often single-source, concentrated in Taiwan, China and Thailand, plus tariff exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: We are solely reliant on contract manufacturers for all of our manufacturing needs.

risks.finding: The company previously had material weaknesses (FY21–FY24). They are now remediated, but could recur. Risks are flagged around last-mile partners and inventory counts.
risks.evidence_quote: we identified certain material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting.

risks.finding: Demand forecasting and inventory risk have led to write-downs and disputes with suppliers over purchase commitments.
risks.evidence_quote: We have in recent periods experienced, and may continue to experience decreases in consumer demand, resulting in inventory write-downs

red_flags.evidence_quote: We have been and in some cases continue to be subject to class action litigation, private personal injury claims and other regulatory proceedings

rating_rationale: Peloton's first annual profit ($63.2M), rising cash ($1.21B), lower debt and effective internal controls are positives. They are offset by two years of falling revenue, liabilities above assets, $1.33B of debt, and ongoing recall-related litigation, including a new Bike+ recall. The 10-K discloses no going concern doubt, no current material weakness, no restatement and no auditor change (EY remains the auditor). Past material weaknesses (FY21–FY24) were remediated.
open_questions: Read Note 12 for the size of recall-related litigation accruals and the status of class actions and CPSC matters, including the Nov 2025 Bike+ recall costs.
Is the FY26 profit driven by cost cuts or one-time items? Check operating income and free cash flow.
What are the trends in subscriptions and churn behind the revenue decline?
Check the covenant headroom on the $1.2B subscription revenue test and how the company plans to refinance the 2029 maturities.
Confirm the stockholders' deficit and the quality of the remediation of earlier material weaknesses, including controls over last-mile partners and shared services.
